bansan.title: 晩餐
bansan.author: 素木しづ
bansan.blurb: A young couple feed their baby at supper while a storm blows outside, and one bad mouthful sends the mother somewhere far away.
bansan.about: Shiraki Shizu wrote this short sketch in 1917, the year before she died. A narrow room, a laughing child, a cold potato; and in a few lines the mother sees her three years of marriage as a whole long life, and a quiet peace waiting at the end of it.

shuchu.title: 酒虫
shuchu.author: 芥川龍之介
shuchu.blurb: A rich man who can drink all day and never get drunk lets a foreign monk tie him up in the summer sun, to draw out the worm in his belly that is doing the drinking.
shuchu.about: Akutagawa Ryūnosuke wrote this in 1916, retelling a tale from Pu Songling's Chinese collection Strange Tales from a Chinese Studio. He tells it with a straight face and a mock-scholarly air, and ends by offering three different answers to what the worm really was.
